title: Improve quantized kernels: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant fusion and scheduling
author: Ethan Park
description: Motivation: Reduce per-token cost and end-to-end latency for common LLM inference workloads by shipping optimized INT8/FP8 kernel paths and fusing dequantization with GEMM/attention kernels. This PR implements a set of runtime and kernel changes: 1) high-throughput INT8 GEMM and FP8 matmul kernels with AVX/AMX/SM80 specializations where available; 2) smoothquant calibration and per-model profiling hooks to compute channel-wise scale factors at load time; 3) operator fusion to eliminate explicit dequantize buffers by sinking dequantization into the compute kernels for attention and feed-forward layers; 4) scheduler/policy updates to prefer quantized kernels when hardware capability flags and model profiles indicate safe accuracy bounds; 5) KV-cache ordering fix for quantized attention to preserve cache invariants across batched requests. The description below summarizes design, test results, compatibility, rollout and follow-ups. Design summary: smoothquant calibration is implemented as an optional model preprocessing step that stores per-channel scales in the model artifact; at runtime the loader applies these scales to produce a mixed INT8/FP8 layout where channel scales are fused into weight metadata. New kernels accept a fused-quant descriptor and perform on-the-fly dequantization inside the GEMM/attention loop to avoid materializing large FP32 intermediates. For FP8 we reuse the existing quantization helpers and add narrow-path microkernels optimized for sequence lengths <= 1024. Scheduler changes: dispatch prefers quantized kernels for routes with throughput SLOs and validated accuracy; fallbacks to FP16/FP32 are automatic on unsupported hardware or if model profile absent. Tests and benchmark summary: microbenchmarks (decoder-only and encoder-decoder configs) show median throughput improvements of +15% to +28% on A100/MI250-class hardware for typical sequence lengths, and p50 latency reduction of 10-18ms on 2048-token workloads. End-to-end regression tests include unit coverage for quantized ops, integration tests with KV-cache, and an automated perf CI that runs representative traces. Compatibility and safety: feature guarded behind capability flags and a model opt-in field; default behavior is unchanged for existing models. Accuracy checks: built-in eval harness compares logits on a calibration set and rejects auto-deploy if delta exceeds thresholds (configurable). Rollout plan: staged rollout via canary percentage in Dedicated and Hosted, followed by Gradual default enablement after two-week telemetry window. Related work items: ENG-2345 and ENG-2401. Notes: initial CI run exposed a flaky microbenchmark which caused bench-ci to fail; addressed by stabilizing timing harness and adding more iterations. Follow-ups: expand FP8 kernels to 8-bit E4 format support and add autotuning for kernel tile sizes.

review_comments: Ava Chen: Overall looks good; please add a safety gate for models that have not been profiled and document the opt-in/opt-out flags. Author reply: Added capability flags and model opt-in field; updated docs.
Marcus Green: Can we add a microbenchmark for sequence lengths 512 and 4096 to ensure edge-case behavior? Author reply: Added benchmarks and results to bench/quant_kernels_bench.py.
Priya Nair: Concern about numerical drift for FP8 on edge cases. Author reply: Added accuracy delta checks and calibration thresholds; default remains conservative.

Diego Alvarez: Scheduler change looks safe but verify that Dedicates autoscaler doesn't route workloads incorrectly. Author reply: Verified with dedicated integration test and added a canary rollout plan.
Performance CI: bench-ci initially failed due to timing harness flakiness on the CI workers; stabilized harness and reran, all perf checks passed.
release_notes: Performance: Improved INT8/FP8 quantized kernel throughput by up to 25% on common LLM workloads. Added smoothquant calibration flow and fused dequant+GEMM/attention kernels to reduce memory traffic. Scheduler now prefers quantized kernels when safe; automatic fallbacks to FP16/FP32 remain. Backwards compatible and opt-in per-model by default.
